narrative:
The model estimated an 82% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. For admissions, that high failure risk is why your application was denied: your file was treated as unlikely to meet the school’s expected bar-passage standard.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That very low rank pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second factor was your LSAT score of 26, well below the accepted-student average of about 37, and it also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your undergraduate GPA of 2.80, below the accepted average of 3.23; in the model’s overall weighing, this was the only one of the top three factors that worked in your favor, modestly moving the estimate toward passing. Even so, your third-year standing and LSAT score outweighed that positive signal. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve a future application, focus on the areas that drove this result: retake the LSAT if you can raise it substantially, seek advising about your third-year academic record, and strengthen your application with additional coursework or evidence of readiness for law study. Reapply only when those credentials show clear improvement.
